title: Manual Handling — Moving Tables & Furniture
blurb: How to shift tables, chairs and furniture for events safely, even under time pressure.
siteNotes: Where trolleys are kept and what each is rated to carry
The maximum safe stack height for chairs
Where fire exits and keep-clear walkways are in each function room
legalNotes: Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992, regs. 4 and 5. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1992/2793
Staff duty to take reasonable care: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, s.7.
Fire exits and escape routes kept clear: Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, art. 14. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2005/1541
No weights or stack heights are quoted, because the trainer gives none; the stack height is left to the venue (see siteNotes).

cards.title: Manual Handling — Moving Tables & Furniture
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- plan a lift and a route before you move anything
- use good technique every time
- store furniture without blocking exits

cards.title: Time pressure is the danger
cards.body: Setting up and turning around function rooms means shifting a lot of tables, chairs and furniture, often against the clock before a wedding or event. That is exactly when people rush, lift badly and hurt themselves. A calm, planned approach keeps you injury-free and actually gets the room ready faster.

cards.title: Check the weight and plan the route
cards.body: Check the weight and think it through. Heavy round tables and stacks of chairs are two-person or trolley jobs. Do not haul them solo to prove a point.

cards.title: Fingers, toes and control
cards.body: Watch your fingers and toes when you set things down. Put items down squarely and under control, not dropped the last few inches.

left.title: Do
items: Stay in control to the floor

right.title: Do not
items: Drop it the last few inches

cards.title: Safe stacks, clear exits
cards.body: Keep stacks at a safe height so they do not topple. Never block fire exits or walkways with stored gear, even just for a minute. Do not overload trolleys.

left.title: Do
items: Keep stacks at a safe height

right.title: Do not
items: Block a fire exit "just for a minute"
Overload a trolley to save time

cards.title: Spread the effort
cards.body: Pace yourself through a big set-up. Spreading the effort protects your back and keeps the whole team going strong all day.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Check the weight, then use help or a trolley
- Plan a clear, dry route first
- Load close, knees bent, back straight, never twist
- Never block fire exits, even for a minute
- Pace yourself through a big set-up

cards.q: Before lifting a table, the first thing to check is its…
cards.why: Check the weight and think it through before you lift.

cards.q: Heavy tables and chair stacks are best moved with help or a trolley.
cards.why: They are two-person or trolley jobs. Do not haul them solo.

cards.q: What should you do about your route before carrying furniture?
options: Work it out as you go
Ask a guest to move out of the way
Plan it and make sure it is clear and dry
Take the shortest way, even if cluttered
cards.why: Plan the route first so it is clear, dry and free of trip hazards.

cards.q: You should keep the load close to your body.
cards.why: Keeping the load close is one of the basics every time.

cards.q: To turn while carrying furniture you should…
cards.why: Never twist. Move your feet to turn instead.

cards.q: It's fine to block a fire exit with furniture "just for a minute".
cards.why: Never block fire exits or walkways with stored gear, even for a minute.

cards.q: When setting an item down you should watch your…
cards.why: Watch your fingers and toes, and put items down squarely and under control.

cards.q: Overloading a trolley is a good way to save time.
cards.why: Do not overload trolleys. It is unsafe and does not save time.

cards.q: Why should you pace yourself during a big set-up?
options: To look busy for the manager
To protect your back and keep going all day
To finish before the other team
To avoid being asked to help
cards.why: Spreading the effort protects your back and keeps the team going strong all day.

cards.q: Chair stacks should be kept at a safe height so they don't topple.
cards.why: Safe stack heights stop stacks toppling onto people.
